title: Can A Society of Generative Agents Simulate Human Behavior and Inform Public Health Policy? — A Case Study on Vaccine Hesitancy

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the initial vaccine hesitancy levels of LLM agents against real-world survey data to identify over-confident biases favoring vaccination acquired from pre-training and safety fine-tuning.

Qualitatively analyzing LLM-generated agents to determine how assigned political beliefs (e.g., Republican vs. Democrat) influence their simulated vaccine hesitancy, cognitive resistance, and responses to public health policies.
Evaluating the consistency and behavioral differences in simulated vaccine attitudes across agent personas varying by age, education level, religion, and other sociodemographic proxies.
